conclusion: Connection reuse reduced hosted peek latency. The snapshot patch did not materially reduce fresh-sandbox Git capture; the sub-two-second cold-read goal remains unmet.
limitations: Three fresh-sandbox samples per version and two warm samples after the first repeated call; these are small samples, not latency percentiles or a service-level objective.
The instrumented fresh/repeated probe excludes launcher and Node startup. Installed CLI measurements include both. Do not combine these measurement boundaries.
All fresh-session trace timelines verify a distinct logical session and Sandbox allocation during the request. Host storage, backend caches, Edge isolates, and service processes were not reset.

Release qualification and smoke tests can warm Edge/service caches. The first three after fresh samples had cached Fleet transports. The separate post-idle sample observed 146.1ms of Fleet setup on workspace inspection, followed by a cache hit on inventory.

The first baseline fresh sample includes a 278ms token refresh; the separate post-idle after sample includes a 354ms token refresh. Subtracting either is an approximation, not an independently measured no-refresh run.
Git capture remains a combined duration; subprocess startup, filesystem metadata, content reads, conversions, object writes, and consistency checks are not separately instrumented on the hosted VM.
Activation-and-binding includes more than VM boot. Snapshot durations are inside handler/request durations and must not be added to them.

The same existing workspace and local checkout at release commit 93d589c were used before and after. The probes requested no workspace file writes and stopped only their own disposable inspection sessions.
Exit 2 with a rendered comparison is retained in all samples; this workspace has excluded entries. It is not a failed HTTP request.
operationalNotes: Both PRs and the 0.3.3 version bump passed CI. All four native archives passed qualification for the exact release commit/runtime.
Tag workflow 40009570400 reused qualified artifacts but skipped publication. The exact verified archives, checksums and installer were published directly without replacing a published version.

The known legacy deployment lacked the new release-control endpoint. The first promotion used a pinned operator check against its exact deployment ID and CLI 0.3.2; ordinary generation checks applied after service promotion.

The provider API component stalled at artifact_verifying while the runtime image succeeded. Restarting only the durable control worker let API attempt 2 succeed; live app sandboxes were not restarted by that service restart.
The Fleet CLI omitted expiry metadata for an unchanged API principal. Its original valid expiry was restored for resumption; credentials were not extended or replaced.

The new deployment was verified with authenticated Vercel CLI access and explicitly promoted because automatic custom-domain assignment is disabled. A brief alias propagation delay required one retry.
No full production environment export was performed. Existing application/database secrets remained in Vercel.
